heading: Connectivity, page visibility and preferences
body:
Three small browser APIs tell a Tac service about the browser: `Connectivity` (is the browser online?), `PageVisibility` (is the page shown?) and `Preferences` (the color scheme, the motion setting and the language). A service reads the current value with a call, and hears each change as a built-in event model.

| API | JavaScript, TypeScript | Rust | Go, C#, F# | Dart, Java, Kotlin, Swift | Ruby | Lua | Event model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connectivity | `@Needs connectivity`, `online()` | `connectivity: Connectivity`, `online()` | `Online()` | `online()` | `Connectivity.new.online` | `Connectivity:online()` | `ConnectivityChanged { online }` |
| PageVisibility | `@Needs pageVisibility`, `visible()` | `page_visibility: PageVisibility`, `visible()` | `Visible()` | `visible()` | `PageVisibility.new.visible` | `PageVisibility:visible()` | `VisibilityChanged { visible }` |
| Preferences | `@Needs preferences`, `scheme()`, `motion()`, `language()` | `preferences: Preferences`, same names | `Scheme()`, `Motion()`, `Language()` | same as JavaScript | `Preferences.new.scheme` | `Preferences:scheme()`, `motion()`, `language()` | `PreferencesChanged { scheme, motion, language }` |

`scheme` is `light` or `dark`, `motion` is `reduce` or `no-preference`, and `language` is the language of the browser, such as `fr-FR`. The service fields are created the same way as `Clock` (see above): Rust fields that `Default` fills, Go `// @Needs` fields, C# `new()` fields, F# `let connectivity = Connectivity()` bindings, Kotlin `Connectivity()` fields, Java `private final Connectivity connectivity = new Connectivity();` fields, Swift `private let connectivity = Connectivity()` fields and Dart `@Needs()` fields. Lua calls the global tables with `:`, such as `Connectivity:online()`, and needs no field. In Swift, a call can throw, so call it with `try`. In F#, the event models are F# records with the C# names, so a listener reads `changed.Online`.

The event models are built in: do not declare them in `client/models/`. Write a listener with a parameter of the model type, like any `@OnEvent` listener. The page publishes the current values when it starts and keeps them, so a listener with `replay` hears the current value first and then every change. These APIs need no permission, so the manifest grants nothing for them. Python has no tab: a Python service has no browser APIs yet, and a Python service that uses one stops the build with `TY1605`.
